sources.locator: "Mozambican War of Independence", revision 1374663244, lead and "Aftermath"

explanation: The article's lead says that "according to historians of the Revolution, the military coup in Portugal was in part fueled by protests concerning the conduct of Portuguese troops in their treatment of some of the indigenous Mozambican populace", and that "the growing communist influence within the group of Portuguese insurgents who led the military coup and the pressure of the international community in relation to the Portuguese Colonial War were the primary causes of the outcome". The body adds that "dissatisfaction in Portugal culminated on 25 April 1974, when the Carnation Revolution, a peaceful leftist military coup d'état in Lisbon, ousted the incumbent Portuguese government of Marcelo Caetano". That is contribution to a cause and not a condition made available, so `caused` is the type, and it is the type this atlas already carries from the Angolan and Guinean openings of the same war. Probable, for the reason every edge drawn from this source is: one article, however careful, is not a literature.
